judged_text: deleteEvent has the same dead fallback: `find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)` is only evaluated when externalCalendarId is falsy, compares against undefined, and returns undefined so calendarId is undefined. Cancellation flows that delete a calendar event without an externalCalendarId now pass calendarId undefined to calendar.events.delete — the remote event is never deleted (or the call errors), leaving orphaned calendar events on every such cancellation.

Cancellation flows that delete a calendar event without an externalCalendarId now pass calendarId undefined to calendar.events.delete — the remote event is never deleted (or the call errors), leaving orphaned calendar events on every such cancellation.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts`, both `updateEvent` and `deleteEvent` compute a fallback calendar ID as `event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)?.externalId` when `externalCalendarId` is falsy (see the ternaries at `selectedCalendar` / `calendarId`). When `externalCalendarId` is falsy, that `find` compares against `undefined` (or `null`), so it will almost always return `undefined`, yielding an undefined `calendarId`. This is a real logic error introduced by the diff; the intended fallback should likely use the first destination calendar (as done elsewhere via `[mainHostDestinationCalendar]`) or match by credentialId, not compare against a missing externalCalendarId.
